dev_notes: src/commands/write.mjs cmdAdd. The payload is JSON on stdin or --file, with flags overriding individual fields; --dry-run prints the file it would write. One file per feature at .ledger/features/<id>.json.

history.name: Recording a capability
history.description: The command ledger add records one capability, with the audience it matters to, its size, its name and a present-tense description of what the product does. The id you give it is lower-case kebab-case and never changes, so it carries the feature's history through every later rename. An entry filed under an area or a sub-section that doesn't exist is refused as you write it, and the message lists the ones that do.

The command ledger add records one capability: who it matters to, its size, its name, a present-tense description, and how a reader sees it for themselves. Its id never changes, so it carries the feature's history through every rename, and an area that doesn't exist is refused with a list of the ones that do.
history.how_to_see: Run ledger add with a how_to_see field in its JSON, then ledger show with the same id: the How to see it line prints what you gave.

events.what: A new capability can say how to see it: the instructions a client follows to check it.
events.why: So a client can check each claim for themselves.
